evidence.excerpt:
Agent memory systems are increasingly evaluated against RAG and full-context
baselines, but reported gains often mix changes in the memory method with changes
in the language model, embedding model, or retrieval pipeline, making it unclear
what is actually being measured. We presentMemDelta, a controlled evaluation
protocol that varies one component at a time on LongMemEval-S (500 questions,
50+ sessions, three model families). Four findings emerge: (1) verbatim RAG
matches full-context GPT-4o-mini (47.2% vs. 49.8%, p= 0.34), but the ranking
reverses across models: Gemini gains +14pp from full context, while Sonnet
gains +31pp from RAG, partly because it refuses 63% of full-context queries;
(2) swapping only the embedding model in an identical pipeline shifts accuracy
by +6.2pp at n= 500 (p= 0.004 ), and Mem0 beats MiniLM-RAG by +11pp
but loses to cloud-RAG by 1.2pp, so one variable

gap we identify is methodological: the field lacks a protocol that varies one component at a time,
holds the rest fixed, and reports whether observed differences survive a significance test.
We presentMemDelta, a controlled evaluation protocol for agent memory systems. The protocol is
deliberately simple: vary one component at a time while holding the rest of the pipeline fixed. We
apply this principle to four common sources of hidden variation, shown in Figure 1: retrieval quality,
embedding choice, language-model behavior, and write-path cost. Retrieval quality asks whether the
relevant evidence is actually surfaced. Embedding choice asks whether a reported memory gain is
instead a better vector representation. Model behavior asks whether the generator uses, ignores, or
refuses the supplied evidence. Write-path cost asks whether a memory system's advantage comes

evidence.excerpt:
Table 1 defines the seven strategies, ordered by write-path complexity. Each receives the same user
history and evaluation questions; they differ only in how prior information is made available to the
answering model.
Three design choices deserve explanation. First, S1 (full context) is not intended as a practical
deployment strategy; it is a diagnostic control that removes retrieval as a bottleneck, allowing us
to measure whether a model can use information when it is explicitly present. Second, S4b is
byte-identical to S4 except for the embedding model. The chunking, top-k, vector-store code, prompt
template, answer model, and judge are all held fixed. Any accuracy difference between S4 and S4b
is therefore attributable to embedding quality alone. Third, S3 (Mem0) uses OpenAI embeddings
4

evidence.excerpt:
Varied:base model (GPT-4o-mini, Sonnet, Gemini).Fixed:strategy, data, judge.
The same S1-vs-S4 comparison yields three qualitatively different conclusions. On GPT-4o-mini,
they are indistinguishable (p= 0.34). On Gemini Flash, full context wins by +14pp. On Sonnet,
retrieval wins by+31pp.
A paper evaluated on a single model would draw a confident conclusion, and that conclusion would
be different depending on which model was chosen.
Sonnet's length-driven failure.63% (188/300) of Sonnet's full-context errors are explicit refusals:
"I don't see this in our conversation history," despite the answer being present in the 115K-token
context. A truncated-context control (∼47K tokens) reduces refusals from 63% to 41% and raises
accuracy from 14% to 38%, consistent with a length-driven attention failure. Even at 47K, Sonnet
trails RAG (61%).
The refusal pattern is not uniform across question

evidence.excerpt:
Varied:embedding model (MiniLM → cloud).Fixed:retrieval code, chunking, data, answer model,
judge.
Switching embeddings within an otherwise identical pipeline raises accuracy from 47.2% to 53.4%
(+6.2pp, p= 0.004). The gains are largest on temporal ( +10.5pp), multi-session (+11.3pp), and
single-session-user (+11.4pp). The direction is not uniform: cloud embeddings underperform on
SS-Asst and SS-Pref.
This is a hidden confound in memory comparisons. A single component swap, costing nothing on the
write path, produces gains comparable to those attributed to architectural changes. Papers comparing
systems with different embeddings may be confounding embedding quality with architecture.
Qualitative examples.The embedding effect is concrete: it changes which passages are retrieved,
and thus which answers are correct. For the question "How long is your daily commute?" (ground
truth: 45

All accuracy judgments use GPT-4o-mini with a binary prompt: given the ground-truth answer and
the model's response, output YES if the response contains the correct information, NO otherwise.
The judge does not see the question context or memory, only the ground truth and the candidate
answer. This avoids inflating scores for verbose but incorrect responses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcomes are established by ground-truth answer matching under a fixed judge prompt, paired statistical testing, and cross-model-family replications rather than by any signal used to shape the systems.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Correctness is scored by GPT-4o-mini using a fixed binary prompt against ground-truth answers, with paired McNemar tests and bootstrap confidence intervals.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No system under study is trained, tuned, or reward-adapted in this work; the compared strategies are fixed off-the-shelf pipelines (verbatim RAG, full context, Mem0, scratchpad) with no in-the-loop optimization against the judge.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that memory gains can be confounded by embedding models, model-specific long-context refusal behaviors, and undisclosed write-path computation are thoroughly corroborated by the controlled experiments and statistical analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical audit evaluates three LLM families (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Flash), reports bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar significance tests, and quantifies write-path computational overhead (time, LLM calls, dollar cost).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on objective ground-truth answer matching, paired statistical tests (McNemar), and cross-model family validations across GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet, and Gemini Flash.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Binary correctness scoring against ground-truth answers using an independent fixed prompt with GPT-4o-mini, complemented by paired McNemar statistical testing.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Fixed off-the-shelf memory architectures, standard RAG pipelines, and pre-trained LLMs evaluated without in-the-loop parameter tuning or reward-driven prompt adaptation.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including restricting the Mem0 comparison to 88 instances across 2 question types due to write-path compute costs, reliance on synthetic benchmark dialogues, and approximate rather than identical embedding matching for Mem0.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology constructs rigorous pairwise comparisons on LongMemEval-S (500 questions), holding prompts, chunking, retrieval logic, and base models constant while varying single components such as embeddings (MiniLM vs OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) and context lengths.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-designed measurement study that cleanly exposes critical methodological confounds in LLM agent memory evaluation with substantial empirical support and controlled statistical contrasts.
primary.scoped_contribution: MemDelta is a controlled empirical evaluation protocol for agent memory systems that isolates retrieval quality, embedding model choice, language model behavior, and write-path cost by varying one factor at a time.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-designed measurement study that cleanly exposes critical methodological confounds in LLM agent memory evaluation with substantial empirical support and controlled statistical contrasts.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including restricting the Mem0 comparison to 88 instances across 2 question types due to write-path compute costs, reliance on synthetic benchmark dialogues, and approximate rather than identical embedding matching for Mem0.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
